process: Whole draft read before scoring; listener pass and macro decisions completed before rewriting.
episode_in_one_sentence: AI moves out of the chat box into background work, playful creations, personal archives, small-business tools, and reproducible scientific tasks.

listener_notes.note: Imagine followed by OpenAI just shipped that turns a hypothetical completed job into a product guarantee; story should lead.
The six matched builds and three-three split are concrete; the third hardware story overlaps Social.
Another model race repeats Marcus's experiment; glasses examples need explicit imaginary framing.
Too many quick finds after the strong archive and chess stories; red-door retrieval is not in the JSON.
A promising local-design opening becomes a catalogue of skills and three scientific repositories.
Four launches becomes eight; the universal usable-today claim is not established by the JSONs.
Lamp, doorbell, and timer examples sound like reported demos; swimming in the koi pond is not sourced.
Dots capabilities and Muse connectors get explained again.
The lab pick's reproduced references and fixed grading are strong, but preliminary paper roundups crowd it.
Repeats the weekly chore, model race, and lab exercise and adds a fourth try.

macro_decisions: Open directly on Dots with a question; keep the CompMat-Bench tease brief.
Keep the seven desks in their original opportunity-first order.
Limit each desk to three substantive stories; Research's short reality check is an explicit exception.
Make archive queries, glasses use cases, and hardware ideas unmistakably hypothetical.
Retain only source-supported product examples and lightly attributed company claims.
Move the scientific video to YouTube; retain Openclatura on Builders for cross-desk science value.

Give Dots to Marcus, model-release economics to Priya, personal archive and chess to Sam, local tools to Maya, consumer launches to Diego, creative showcase and hardware to Lena, scientific papers and lab pick to Aaron.
Use distinct handbacks that still include back to you, satisfying the script skill's validation.
Keep the lab pick at roughly 60–90 seconds and the reality check at roughly 45–75 seconds.
Close with three new applications of covered capabilities and three opportunity-focused watch questions.
Keep the episode between 18 and 24 minutes at 155 words per minute; do not add facts to fill time.
